solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Evil sort of long-term prisoner holding copper back (7)

indicators.note: the lifer holds the copper inside him
the copper symbol is read backwards

blocks.note: a lifer is serving a life sentence
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

annotation.surface: A hardened lifer who has taken a police officer hostage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman in the surface, but it is the metal, symbol Cu, turned round to UC before going in.
annotation.definitionFit: Lucifer, the Devil, is the evil sort par excellence.

entries.clue: Large doctor breaking one’s legs? (5)

definitions.note: legs are an example of limbs, hence the question mark

indicators.note: the doctor breaks into the middle of I'S

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing labels
one = I, plus the S of 's

annotation.surface: A hefty doctor snapping somebody's legs, a grim picture.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks legs as just one kind of limb, a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: legs are one pair of the body's four limbs, so the question mark flags a part standing for the class.

entries.clue: Arian is cast in more concise preliminary dramatic piece (7-6)

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, and so to shape afresh
the mixed letters go inside CURTER

blocks.note: curt = brief, so curter = more concise

annotation.surface: A theatre note: an actor named Arian is cast in a shorter play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cast' fits the theatre surface as choosing an actor, which hides its job of rearranging the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A curtain-raiser is a short piece staged before the main play.

entries.clue: Female is not commonly dim (5)

blocks.note: ain't is the informal form of 'is not'

annotation.surface: A slangy retort that a woman is not stupid.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dim' reads as stupid in the surface; here it means barely visible.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of barely visible or weak, not the 'stupid' sense the surface suggests.

entries.clue: Concerning fast, give in (6)

blocks.note: re = concerning, as in memo headers
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

annotation.surface: Someone on a fast tempted to give up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adjective for speed but is the noun, a period of fasting.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean yielding after first holding out against something.

entries.clue: Nine divine sisters, married, with needs (5)

annotation.surface: Nine holy sisters, now married and with needs of their own.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Needs' is a noun here: uses, as in 'has no uses for it'.
annotation.definitionFit: The nine Muses of Greek myth were the divine daughters of Zeus.

entries.clue: Ideal man’s power to accommodate bishop (2,5)

indicators.note: MIGHT gives the bishop a room inside it

blocks.note: RR = Right Reverend, a bishop's title

annotation.surface: A perfect man with the influence to put up a bishop.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has', linking definition to wordplay. RR, Right Reverend, is the form of address for a Church of England bishop.
annotation.definitionFit: Mr Right is the ideal partner someone hopes to meet.

entries.clue: Slipshod head of programming ain’t developing attention to neatness (4,3,6)

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
the letters develop into a new form

annotation.surface: A sloppy coding team lead who isn't learning to be tidy.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is the opposite of 'slipshod', which is the joke: the careless word supplies the letters for care.
annotation.definitionFit: Spit and polish means scrupulous cleaning and smartness, as of a soldier's boots.

entries.clue: Convince Express about The Independent’s sports features, primarily (7)

indicators.note: SAY goes round the letters
the first letter of each of the words

blocks.note: first letters of The, Independent's, Sports, Features

annotation.surface: One newspaper, the Express, trying to win readers over with a rival's sports pages.
annotation.walkthrough: The two newspaper names look like a media story; the Express is just 'say', and The Independent only lends its initials.
annotation.definitionFit: A less familiar sense: 'satisfy the court that…' means persuading beyond doubt, not pleasing.

entries.clue: Combatant’s violent alarmist trait (7,6)

indicators.note: the letters are violently thrown about

annotation.surface: A fighter whose aggressive streak alarms everyone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Violent' suits a fighter so well in the surface that it hardly reads as an instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A martial artist, a practitioner of karate or judo, is a combatant.

entries.clue: Very strict role in Sid and Nancy to begin with (7)

indicators.note: PART sits inside the initials
take the beginning of each word

blocks.clueFragment: Sid and Nancy to begin with
blocks.note: first letters of Sid, And, Nancy
a role is a part in a play or film

annotation.surface: An actor's harsh part in the film Sid and Nancy.
annotation.walkthrough: Sid and Nancy is a 1986 film about Sid Vicious and Nancy Spungen, which makes 'role' feel like part of the story.
annotation.definitionFit: Spartan means austere and strict, like life in ancient Sparta.

entries.clue: Grand young woman, one that can hold a drink (5)

definitions.text: one that can hold a drink

annotation.surface: A fine young woman who can hold her drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface says she copes well with alcohol; the definition means a vessel that literally holds one.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the tumbler or wine vessel literally holds liquid, turning the surface's boast about tolerance into plain fact.

entries.clue: Scandinavian article about depression? On the contrary (6)

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other
swap the roles: the depression goes round the article

blocks.note: a dish is a hollow or depression

annotation.surface: A Nordic newspaper piece on depression.
annotation.walkthrough: Read literally, the article would go round the depression; 'On the contrary' swaps who holds whom. A dish is a hollow in the ground, as in a radio dish.
annotation.definitionFit: Danish means from Denmark, a Scandinavian country.

entries.clue: British dame hosting priest and southern composer (7)

indicators.note: DBE hosts the priest inside it
'and' means plus, so the southern letter is simply tacked on after the rest

blocks.note: DBE = Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire
Eli, the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

annotation.surface: A British dame entertaining a clergyman and a composer from the south.
annotation.walkthrough: A DBE is the honour that makes a woman a dame. Léo Delibes was the French composer of the ballet Coppélia.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the French writer of the ballets Coppélia and Sylvia is one example of a composer.

entries.clue: Tabloid space that could offer a bright perspective (7)

definitions.text: that could offer a bright perspective
definitions.note: read as 'a place that could offer a bright perspective'

blocks.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

annotation.surface: A column in a tabloid meant to cheer readers up.
annotation.walkthrough: The Sun is Britain's best-selling tabloid. 'Bright perspective' sounds like optimism but means a sunny view out of the windows.
annotation.definitionFit: A sunroom is a glass-walled room letting in light and views.

entries.clue: Heavy old dog disheartened in pen (6)

indicators.note: the heart, the middle letter, is removed
the pieces sit inside the pen

blocks.note: a sty is a pig pen

annotation.surface: A fat old dog, downcast in its enclosure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' reads as sad, but a word's heart is its middle letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, used of food that sits in the stomach, or of dull, ponderous writing.

entries.clue: Adhesive containing trace of this new protein (6)

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so the adhesive's letters wrap round the T
a trace of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A fresh glue that contains a hint of protein.
annotation.walkthrough: Gluten is also what makes dough sticky, so the glue in the surface is not far off.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the stretchy substance in wheat flour is one particular protein.

entries.clue: Gain knowledge from, off and on, illegal service (5)

indicators.note: letters are skipped and taken in turn

blocks.note: iLlEgAl: second, fourth and sixth letters
RN = Royal Navy, one of the services

annotation.surface: Picking up tips now and then from some illicit trade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like a job done for money, but the armed services give RN, the Royal Navy.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'from' goes with the definition as in learning from a teacher.

entries.clue: Spend a lot on French version of The Scream (4,3)

annotation.surface: Paying a fortune for a French copy of Munch's painting The Scream.
annotation.walkthrough: The Scream looks like Munch's famous painting but is just the verb, and 'The' alone is the word being translated.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom: besides hitting out, it means splashing money about extravagantly.

entries.clue: Small mammal, quiet, on top of woodpile (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A little animal sitting silently on a stack of logs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' reads as position in the surface, but it supplies RE, meaning about or concerning.
annotation.definitionFit: A shrew is a tiny insect-eating mammal.

entries.clue: Mathematician almost finds Italian city (5)

indicators.note: the word stops one letter short

blocks.note: Alan TURING without his last letter

annotation.surface: A mathematician nearly discovering an Italian city.
annotation.walkthrough: Alan Turing was the British mathematician behind wartime codebreaking and early computing.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the Piedmont capital, home of Fiat and Juventus, is one Italian city.

entries.clue: Inert sort unexpectedly bitten by Dutch South African dog (6,7)

indicators.note: the letters come out in an unexpected order
the Boer's teeth close round the mixed letters

blocks.note: the Boers were Dutch-descended settlers in South Africa

annotation.surface: A lazy type suddenly bitten by a South African's dog.
annotation.walkthrough: The dog seems to belong to the South African; it is in fact the definition, and the Boer is the wrapper.
annotation.definitionFit: The Boston terrier is a small American breed of dog.

entries.clue: Starts to spray crowd with drink, causing disorderly struggle (5)

indicators.note: take the start of each word

annotation.surface: Someone showering a crowd with booze and starting a brawl.
annotation.walkthrough: In rugby a scrum is a set piece, but the word also means any disorderly crush.
annotation.definitionFit: A scrum is a disorderly crowd pushing and struggling.

entries.clue: Mild rebuke, not when partly backtracking (3,4)

indicators.note: only part of the phrase, the T and W, turns back

annotation.surface: A gentle telling-off that stops short of saying when.
annotation.walkthrough: Write NOT WHEN and swap the adjacent T and W: that small reversal in the middle is the only change.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Now then!' is a mild way of telling someone off.
